summary: Wrote a 5-phase, 7.5-hour plan for the re-anchored deletion half: a z-anchored lift (Phase 1), a register-exposing deletion theorem under an explicit anchor clause (Phase 2), a decision gate collapsing the clause to the first region start and attempting the residual inequality (Phase 3), the branch-selected single-block downward assembly (Phase 4), and record plus full gate (Phase 5). Two authoring-time findings shape it: every new declaration goes in LadderChain.lean because LadderPump.lean is upstream of the lift and at the longFile ceiling, and the residual inequality's upper direction has no landed source (Drift permits a climbing register), so the FAIL branch with a named forward-slack hypothesis is fully specified. Both pinned Challenge statements were elaborated standalone against the built library.
